title: TaskFlow -> Enterprise Systems
outcome: Generalize TaskFlow patterns into larger enterprise systems while preserving modular boundaries, workflows, auditability, integration reliability, and migration paths.
artifact: Enterprise expansion blueprint for an HRIS/procurement/inventory/payroll-style system with modules, workflows, events, audit, and scaling triggers.
labSteps: Choose one enterprise domain and identify business capabilities before choosing services/databases.
Design modules with explicit ownership and public interfaces inside a modular monolith.
Model one long-running approval as a state machine with actors, transitions, evidence, and audit records.
Identify a transaction that crosses an integration boundary and design an outbox/event handoff.
Separate synchronous user requests from background work such as reports, imports, notifications, or payroll runs.
Write concrete scaling triggers that would justify extracting a service, queue, cache, or separate database later.
failureModes: Microservices before module boundaries are understood
Boolean fields replacing explicit workflow states
Dual writes to database and message broker without reliability design
Shared database tables with unclear ownership across domains
mastery: Can justify when distribution is and is not earned
principles: Enterprise scaling starts by identifying new business boundaries, compliance needs, load, and organizational ownership.
Keep the modular monolith viable until scale or team boundaries justify distributing the system.
Add queues, caches, services, and orchestration only for concrete bottlenecks or ownership needs.
Design replaceable infrastructure interfaces so managed services can evolve without rewriting core business rules.
